title.narrative: Psychosocial and livelihoods support to victims of psychological suffering in Rwanda

description.narrative:
CDJP Nyundo will centred the programme during this exit period of CAFOD funding around training of APS and volunteers animators who have the apostolate mission of supporting all desadvantaged people within the diocese. Strenghtening their capacities will be a guarantee of the durability of the results and outcomes of the previous projects. The integrated livelihoods aspects are important to maintain the psychological balance - because the trauma is both a physical and health crisis.
After building a pilot “Peace House”, the commission expect the use of this community infrastructure to attend its objectives and train people in trauma and other identified trainings that will contribute in trauma healing; peace and reconciliation and human rights and access to justice promotion. Counselling sessions, a variety of trainings (as for the other Justice and peace commission) and field visits are planned in 2012.
